## 1. Audit — the refutation is correct; I withdraw the AC ≤ s claim

**Hand-verified, enumeration-independent:**

- **Masks/diff-points:** 128 = {7} (AND3); 136 = {3,7}; 160 = {5,7}; 192 = {6,7}; const0 = ∅. Symmetric differences with {7} are exactly {3}, {5}, {6}, {7}. ✓ Lex-first-missing is consistent: 00000000 (const0) realizable, next table 00000001 = mask 128. ✓
- **Realizability:** AND(xi,xj) = NAND(g,g), g = NAND(xi,xj): 2 gates ✓. const0: g1=NAND(x0,x0), g2=NAND(g1,x0) ≡ 1, g3=NAND(g2,g2) ≡ 0: 3 gates ✓ (and no fewer: any NAND of inputs outputs 0 at assignment 7, so ≡1 needs ≥2 gates, ≡0 needs ≥3).
- **AND3 ∉ SIZE(3) (premise; proof):** output NAND(u,v) forces u∧v ≡ ¬AND3, i.e. u=v=1 on assignments 0–6, u(7)∧v(7)=0. At assignment 0 all inputs are 0, so u,v are gates. If u=v, then ¬AND3 = NAND(c,d) with c∧d ≡ AND3 in ≤2 gates: two inputs give a 2-var AND ≠ AND3, and any gate is 0 at assignment 7 while c(7)=d(7)=1 is required — impossible. So u≠v, both gates; with the output that uses all 3 gates, and one of u,v must be the bottom gate g1 = NAND(a,b) over inputs. But every variable pair (or repeated variable) is simultaneously 1 at some assignment ≤ 6, so g1 has a 0 in 0–6. Contradiction. ∎
- **Forcing:** each of the four functions lies in SIZE(3) and agrees with AND3 off its single diff-point, so any distinguishing set A omitting one of 3,5,6,7 fails. Hence min |A| ≥ 4 > 3. This is **robust to enumerator bugs**: it uses only the four hand-built circuits and the hand-proved missingness; extra realizable functions only raise the minimum.

**Unverified but immaterial:** the counts 22359 (encoding-convention-dependent; I cannot reproduce it without your exact description grammar) and 48 tables; and exact sufficiency of A={3,5,6,7} (i.e. min = 4, not just ≥ 4) rests on your exhaustive search — rerunnable. (A does also kill size-0 projections: x0,x1 differ at 3; x2 at 5.)

**Verdict:** no mathematical error found. The universal conjecture "every function missing at size s has a distinguishing set of ≤ s assignments" is **false at (n,s)=(3,3) and is withdrawn**.

## 2. Why finite 4 > 3 does not give ω(s)

"AC = ω(s)" asserts: for every constant c there are infinitely many instances with AC > c·s. The datum is one point with ratio 4/3. It refutes only the ∀-statement with constant 1 and zero additive slack; it is simultaneously consistent with AC ≤ s+1 everywhere, AC ≤ ⌈4s/3⌉, and AC ≤ s for all (n,s) ≠ (3,3). Moreover (3,3) is in the pre-universality regime (48/256 tables): the bound is driven by the four Hamming-distance-1 realizable neighbors of AND3, and nothing in the datum shows that the forced-point count (≈ number of distance-1 realizable neighbors, or its fractional-cover analogue) grows superlinearly in s as n→∞ with s=s(n). Finite counterexamples constrain quantifiers, not growth rates.

## 3. Known-style lemma (provable from standard tools; no literature relied on)

**Lemma (antichecker with Θ(n) slack).** NAND basis, inputs only (universal; constants cost ≤3 gates). Fix γ∈(0,1/2), absolute c₀. If f: {0,1}ⁿ→{0,1} requires size > s and s ≥ c₀n/γ², set s′ = ⌊γ²s/(c₀n)⌋ ≥ 1. Then there is a multiset A, |A| = O(γ⁻² s′ log(n+s′)), such that every circuit of size ≤ s′ disagrees with f on ≥ (1/2−2γ)|A| points. For n ≳ log s this gives |A| ≤ s.

*Sketch:* (i) If some mixed strategy over SIZE(s′) erred < 1/2−γ on every input, majority of t = O(n/γ²) i.i.d. samples errs nowhere (Chernoff + union over 2ⁿ inputs); MAJ_t costs O(t) gates (carry-save adders + comparator), total ts′+O(t) ≤ s — contradiction. Finite minimax (LP duality) yields a distribution D with every size-s′ circuit erring w.p. ≥ 1/2−γ. (ii) Sample m points from D; Chernoff + union over ≤ (n+s′)^{2s′}·2^{O(s′)} circuits gives the multiset. ∎

Note: this gives slack **Θ(n/γ²)** in circuit size and antichecker size Õ(s/n) — it does **not** prove any constant-slack repair.

## 4. ONE repaired statement — Conjecture AC2 (**unproved**)

**AC2:** In this NAND model, for all n ≥ 3, s ≥ 2, and every f ∉ SIZE(s), there exists A with |A| ≤ s such that every circuit of size ≤ ⌊s/2⌋ differs from f on some point of A.

It evades the counterexample: at (3,3) the target class is SIZE(1) ∪ projections, and A = {1,2,4} works (each of x0,x1,x2,¬xi,NAND(xi,xj) takes value 1 on one of 1,2,4, where AND3 ≡ 0). The Lemma supports only Θ(n) slack, so constant slack 2 is a genuine, unproved leap.

**Falsification experiment:** enumerate canonical NAND circuits (dedupe by truth table), n=3, s = 2,…,S until SIZE(S) = all 256 tables. For each s and each missing f, form D_g = diff(f,g) for all g ∈ SIZE(⌊s/2⌋) and solve exact minimum hitting set over the 8-point universe (brute force 2⁸ subsets). AC2 is falsified iff some minimum > s. Extend to n=4, s ≤ 7 (16-point universe, exact ILP/branch-and-bound). Pre-registered quick kill: any missing f with more than s distance-1 neighbors inside SIZE(⌊s/2⌋) refutes AC2 immediately.

## 5. Scope

Nothing here claims or implies NP lower bounds; the Lemma is conditional on the hardness of f, which at these sizes is supplied only by brute-force-verified facts. The qualified residue of the old conjecture — e.g. AC ≤ s+O(1), or AC ≤ s for s ≥ s₀(n) — remains open, untested beyond (3,3). This closes the finite analysis; no bearing on P vs NP is asserted.
